direction: Ruin-priority scoring as a stagnation-adaptive rank-power rule: normalize per-node removal savings by run-scale, multiply load/depot/demand/route-distance gating factors, then rank-transform and raise to an exponent that grows with stagnation_ratio (mild when improving, aggressive when stuck) to diversify destroy sets under the 500 ms anytime budget.

operations.mechanism: KB entry method-cvrp-m3-ruin-recreate-l3 documents the L3 skeleton (CW + intra_2opt + Regret-2 reinsertion + R2R acceptance) with a fixed worst-removal control at 23.3474 mean blind tour length and an evolved multiplicative-gate/rank-power destroy rule at 23.3186, showing the destroy-priority hook is the binding degree of freedom and that the controlled baseline is a solid, feasible-by-2-3 ms starting point. It further notes the evolved rule won 8/24 dev problems over the constructive champion, i.e. per-instance complementarity is real. Since only score_ruin_nodes is evolvable and postprocess must be 'none', the highest-leverage deterministic refinement is (a) scale-free rank normalization of |removal_savings| for cross-instance robustness on heterogeneous demand/geometry, and (b) a stagnation-adaptive power exponent that sharpens or flattens the destroy distribution as the search stalls, directly implementing the 'stagnation_aware_diversification' strong regime flagged in the KB while keeping tie-breaking deterministic. Regret-2 reinsertion plus intra_2opt is retained unchanged so any gain is attributable to the evolved destroy score, preserving the strict attribution separation the KB baseline was built for.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: A rank-based (monotone-invariant) power transform of removal savings with multiplicative gating (gates on route load ratio, depot-adjacency, demand, and route distance) outperforms plain worst-removal scoring on dev_24 hetero instances at 500 ms, because rank normalization removes scale heterogeneity across instances while the stagnation-driven exponent switches from local (small exponent, exploit) to global (large exponent, diversify) destruction without introducing RNG nondeterminism.
